action.new:
Reading the :attr:`port` attribute will raise a :exc:`ValueError` if
   an invalid port is specified in the URL.  The error is raised when
   the :attr:`port` attribute is *accessed*, not when the URL is first
   parsed and the result object is constructed.  The port must be a
   string of one or more ASCII decimal digits representing an integer
   in the range 0--65535 (inclusive).  If the netloc has no colon, or
   the portion after the last colon is empty, the attribute returns
   :const:`None` and no error is raised.

   .. doctest::
      :options: +NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE

      >>> from urllib.parse import urlsplit
      >>> # No port in netloc: .port returns None
      ...
      >>> p = urlsplit("http://example.com/")
      >>> p.port
      None
      >>> # Empty port (trailing colon): .port returns None
      ...
      >>> p = urlsplit("http://example.com:/")
      >>> p.port
      None
      >>> # Lower boundary: port 0 is valid
      ...
      >>> p = urlsplit("http://example.com:0/")
      >>> p.port
      0
      >>> # Upper boundary: port 65535 is valid
      ...
      >>> p = urlsplit("http://example.com:65535/")
      >>> p.port
      65535
      >>> # One above upper bound: ValueError at .port access
      ...
      >>> p = urlsplit("http://example.com:65536/")
      >>> p.port
      Traceback (most recent call last):
        File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
      ValueError: Port out of range 0-65535
      >>> # Negative port: not a digit string, ValueError
      ...
      >>> p = urlsplit("http://example.com:-1/")
      >>> p.port
      Traceback (most recent call last):
        File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
      ValueError: Port could not be cast to integer value as '-1'
      >>> # Non-numeric port: ValueError
      ...
      >>> p = urlsplit("http://example.com:abc/")
      >>> p.port
      Traceback (most recent call last):
        File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
      ValueError: Port could not be cast to integer value as 'abc'
      >>> # Non-ASCII digit (Devanagari zero U+0966): ValueError
      ...
      >>> p = urlsplit("http://example.com:\u0966/")
      >>> p.port
      Traceback (most recent call last):
        File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
      ValueError: Port could not be cast to integer value as '\u0966'

   See section :ref:`urlparse-result-object` for more information on the
   result object.
